sentences.text: 4. As per prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that he abducted the prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in this case.
Statement of the prosecutrix has yet not been recorded before the Trial Court.
Applicant is a young boy aged about 19 years and is in jail since 7.7.2023.
Final conclusion of trial will take a long time.
Under these circumstances, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the custody period of the applicant which is more than ten months, I am of the view that it is a fit case for grant of bail.
Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Sanjay @ Sanju vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44962501/
